text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary traffic ramp to model encoder-q3-quant triggered latency SLO breach. p95=1.2s, p99=2.9s (SLO p99 <= 1.5s). Streaming stalls observed (~0.8% of streams stalled). Root ts=1768523333

deploy-bot: rolling traffic: encoder-q3-quant -> 30% (auto-ramp). started at 2026-03-15T14:12:10Z

SRE-Jess: I’m paging oncall. @Oncall-Mike you oncall? p99 looks rough at tail, streaming stalls callout worries me (stalling while waiting for KV loads?).

Oncall-Mike: here — just woke up to the page. seeing elevated tail in canary region-us-west. digging into per-host p99s.

Infra-Alex: metrics: 3 instances show p99 > 4s, others ~2.5-3s. CPU not saturated, GPU util ~60-70%. KV cache miss spike correlates with stalls.

Marcos-Eng: new quantization path rolled into encoder-q3-quant. It changes kernel ordering and increases on-host memory reads. Could be thrashing L2/L3. Also added a small change to async prefetch last night.

Priya-Prod: customer impact: CS telemetry shows ~0.6% of total prod requests from 4 enterprise tenants hit >5s. Not yet widespread but enough to trigger alerts. Leah from CS on call? @CustomerSuccess-Leah

CustomerSuccess-Leah: confirmed two customers reported slow responses via partner slack; prioritized. Getting early impact details.

SRE-Jess: mitigation options: 1) pause canary ramp (stop at 30%), 2) rollback to encoder-q3-fp16, 3) increase pool size for canary (buy time), 4) force lower batch sizes / limit streaming concurrency. Which should we do first?

Oncall-Mike: immediate: PAUSE ramp and rollback is next if pause doesn't improve within 5-10m. Issuing pause now.

deploy-bot: ACTION: pause_traffic_ramp encoder-q3-quant -> set traffic 30% hold. Command accepted.

SRE-Jess: I'm enabling detailed traces for the 30% canary traffic to capture KV miss stack and latencies. Turning on request-level sampling x100 for canary.

Marcos-Eng: while we monitor traces, quick check: the new prefetch path logs show occasional backpressure errors when concurrent prefetches > 32. That could cause stalls while waiting for IO.

Infra-Alex: also seeing increased host-side swap events on two nodes (minor, but correlated). Might be memory working set increase from quant kernels.

Oncall-Mike: rolling a targeted config: reduce concurrency_on_streaming to 24 for canary via runtime flag. Applying now.

SRE-Jess: applied. Please monitor p99s.

(3m pass)

SRE-Jess: p95 improved to 0.9s, p99 down to 1.9s (from 2.9s). Stalls decreased but still above SLO. KV miss rate still ~1.1x baseline.

Marcos-Eng: thanks. That suggests concurrency bump exacerbated kernel IO pattern. I've got a quick patch to make prefetch backoff more conservative — will build a canary patch but that means another rollout. Prefer rollforward or rollback?

Oncall-Mike: given customer reports, + risk of second rollout, prefer rollback to fp16 stable for immediate relief. Prepare rollback plan and ETA.

Marcos-Eng: prepping rollback artifact now. ETA ~12m to cut traffic and verify.

Priya-Prod: notify customers that we’re aware and mitigations in flight. Leah will coordinate status updates.

CustomerSuccess-Leah: posting to affected customers: "We saw intermittent slow responses for a subset of requests - engineers are rolling back a canary change now and we expect resolution within 20 minutes. Will follow up when fixed."

(10m)

deploy-bot: START: rollback encoder-q3-quant -> encoder-q3-fp16. Rolling traffic from 30% -> 0% over 2 steps.

SRE-Jess: monitoring. Adding heatmap of p99 by hostname.

Infra-Alex: host swap events dropping. KV miss returning to baseline.

(5m)

SRE-Jess: p99 now 1.1s, p95 0.85s. Streaming stalls back to baseline. Looks like rollback fixed it.

Oncall-Mike: good. Closing immediate paging loop. Recommend postmortem and root cause analysis.

Marcos-Eng: taking ownership of RCA. Initial hypothesis: quantization-specific kernel ordering + aggressive prefetch backoff caused increased memory pressure and IO contention for some sequence-length patterns, exposing a tail lat issue under live traffic shapes. Will reproduce with workload replay and incremental test vectors.

Priya-Prod: action items: 1) Marcos to produce detailed RCA and repro test (48h), 2) Eng to add canary traffic CPU/GPU memory working set guardrails (24h), 3) SRE to add alert for swap/host memory anomaly tied to canary population (6h), 4) CS to follow up with customers with post-incident note (ASAP).

CustomerSuccess-Leah: I’ll send closure note to affected customers once final RCA draft is available.

SRE-Jess: moving to incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. I'll create incident ticket and hand off to oncall next shift at 18:00Z. @Oncall-Mike please summarize any outstanding follow-ups before handoff.

Oncall-Mike: Summary for handoff: rollback completed, p99 back within SLO, traces collected for 30% canary window, Marcos reproducing locally. Outstanding: add memory/swap alert, tighten canary concurrency guardrail, confirm prefetch backoff fix. No active customer escalations pending.

SRE-Jess: thanks. Handoff to Night Oncall: please watch for regressions during next ramp and block auto-ramp until eng confirms root cause fix and we have canary guardrails.

deploy-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated (status). Incident ticket: INC-20260315-00123

CustomerSuccess-Leah: customers acknowledged the rollback and appreciate proactive update. Will close the support threads after RCA follow-up. :thumbsup:

Marcos-Eng: starting full replay job now (captures+live traffic sample). Will post logs and a shortened RCA in #eng-runtime when ready.

SRE-Jess: thanks everyone. Marking thread as resolved for paging. Please attach RCA link to INC-20260315-00123 when available.

Oncall-Mike: signing off for handoff. :wave:
__COMMENT: This file is a single Slack thread represented as a continuous string. No title field per agents.md.
